Reel It In sits between you and the slot machine. The Reels tab gets shut down the moment you land on it. Reels your friends share in DMs still work — one reel, one viewing, no autoswipe to the next. Think of it as a dopamine cleanse for your feed.

Reel It In uses Android's Accessibility framework to read the top window when Instagram is in the foreground. The detector identifies:

• The Reels tab (main reels feed) — always blocked.
• A DM thread followed by a reel viewer — the reel is allowed, once.
• Any scroll or swipe to a different reel — blocked.

When blocking triggers, a banner appears and the app routes you back to the last non-Reels Instagram tab when it can, or backs out once from a fullscreen reel viewer.

The point: claim back your attention. Use Instagram to see what your friends are actually up to — not to get brainmaxxed by an algorithm.
